document.title: Afghanistan: [Excised] Criticizes GOP's Afghan Policy; Says It Is Letting Policy Drift
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Confidential] Embassy talks with a source who appears to be former Interior Minister Nasrullah Babar on Pakistan's Afghan policy and border control. Babar notes strengthening Pashtun ties and says he supported deploying ISI officers from the Kabul embassy and from Herat, Kandahar and Jalalabad consulates to advise the Taliban while letting the GOP monitor the ISI.

persons.name: Bill Richardson
persons.role: US Ambassador (to the UN) who visited Afghanistan in April 1997 to kick-start the peace process

mentions.quote: THE EFFORT BY AMBASSADOR RICHARDSON TO KICK START THE PEACE PROCESS DURING HIS APRIL 1997 VISIT TO AFGHANISTAN WAS WORTHWHILE
WITH THE NAWAZ SHARIF GOVERNMENT, THERE HAS NEVER BEEN A SUSTAINED EFFORT TO BRING THE FACTIONS TO THE BARGAINING TABLE

persons.name: Benazir Bhutto
persons.role: Former Prime Minister of Pakistan, in office until November 1996; her government built up the Taliban
persons.status_detail: Government forced from office in November 1996

mentions.quote: THE BHUTTO GOVERNMENT'S [POLICY] IN REGARD TO AFGHANISTAN... WE TRIED TO BUILD THE TALIBAN UP AND THEN TRIED TO PUSH THEM TO NEGOTIATIONS

persons.name: Iftikhar Murshed
persons.role: Additional Secretary, Pakistan MFA; GOP coordinator for Afghan policy

mentions.quote: THE GOP'S COORDINATOR FOR AFGHAN POLICY (MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS ADDITIONAL SECRETARY IFTIKHAR MURSHED) DOES NOT HAVE ENOUGH EXPERTISE

persons.name: Abdul Hamid Afridi
persons.role: Pakistani Foreign Service officer selected as Pakistan's Consul General in Kandahar

mentions.quote: THE GOP, IN FACT, HAD RECENTLY SELECTED ABDUL HAMID AFRIDI, A FOREIGN SERVICE OFFICER, TO BE PAKISTAN'S CONSUL GENERAL IN KANDAHAR

events.description: US Embassy POLOFF meets an excised Pakistani interlocutor, who criticizes GOP Afghan policy and sees a continuing stalemate.
Ambassador Richardson visits Afghanistan to try to kick-start the peace process.
Bhutto government's shuttle diplomacy to push the Taliban to negotiate after they captured Kabul, not implemented because of factional intransigence.
Pakistan agrees to sell 600,000 tons of subsidized wheat to buyers chosen by the Taliban; the price was set too high and the Taliban bought little.
Major Gul, a retired ISI officer, begins serving in Kandahar as Pakistan's consul general.
GOP selects Abdul Hamid Afridi as consul general in Kandahar to replace Major Gul.
US Embassy Islamabad political officer met an excised source who criticized GOP Afghan policy as drifting.
Ambassador Bill Richardson visited Afghanistan to kick-start the peace process.
Taliban captured Kabul; Pakistan pushed them to negotiate.
Bhutto government removed from office, ending shuttle diplomacy.
Pakistan agreed to sell 600,000 tons of subsidized wheat to Taliban-chosen buyers.
GOP selected Abdul Hamid Afridi as Consul General in Kandahar to replace Major Gul.
Major Gul began his posting in Kandahar.

key_claims: The Pakistani government's Afghan policy lacks direction under Nawaz Sharif, in contrast to the coherent Bhutto-era policy of building up the Taliban.
Neither the Taliban nor the northern grouping is ready to negotiate; both believe in a military solution and the stalemate is expected to last at least six months.
The ISI supports the Taliban, which undermines Pakistan's declaratory policy of favoring negotiations.
ISI officers operate from Pakistani diplomatic posts in Kabul, Herat, Kandahar and Jalalabad and advise the Taliban.
Pakistan has failed to control the Afghan border: wheat smuggling continues and the transit trade agreement remains unresolved.
Pakistani and Afghan Pashtuns are drawing closer, which could threaten Afghan sovereignty.
